turns.assessment: The simultaneous OTU_LOF events and near-identical ~68 ps DGD increases across many channels identify a common DGD rise on the S14→S04 optical section. Stable channel power, OSNR, amplifier powers, and pump currents argue strongly against a cut, connector, amplifier, or WSS power fault. The evidence localizes the cause to one of the six fibre spans on that section, but does not distinguish which span, so no individual repair target reaches 80% confidence.

proposals.rationale: Span 1 is on the common S14→S04 optical path and a DGD rise explains the common large DGD step, BER increase, and LOF without a power or OSNR change.
Span 2 is an equally plausible source of the accumulated DGD increase on the common section; available receiver measurements cannot isolate the contributing span.
Span 3 is an equally plausible source of the common DGD increase, with no span-local measurement identifying another segment.
Span 4 is an equally plausible source of the accumulated DGD rise and resulting coherent receiver failures.
Span 5 is an equally plausible source; the unchanged optical power and amplifier telemetry remain consistent with PMD/DGD rather than attenuation.
Span 6 is an equally plausible source of the common DGD step, but there is no evidence that specifically favors this final span.
